title: HUG-VAS: A Hierarchical NURBS-Based Generative Model for Aortic Geometry Synthesis and Controllable Editing

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《HUG-VAS: A Hierarchical NURBS-Based Generative Model for Aortic Geometry Synthesis and Controllable Editing》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Accurate, patient-specific vascular geometry is pivotal for diagnosis, planning, and device design, yet existing statistical shape modeling (SSM) pipelines rely on linear priors and topology-specific preprocessing that limit realism, scalability, and interoperability.

evidence.text: Accurate, patient-specific vascular geometry is pivotal for diagnosis, planning, and device design, yet existing statistical shape modeling (SSM) pipelines rely on linear priors and topology-specific preprocessing that limit realism, scalability, and interoperability.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《HUG-VAS: A Hierarchical NURBS-Based Generative Model for Aortic Geometry Synthesis and Controllable Editing》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Accurate, patient-specific vascular geometry is pivotal for diagnosis, planning, and device design, yet existing statistical shape modeling (SSM) pipelines rely on linear priors and topology-specific preprocessing that limit realism, scalability, and interoperability.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Beyond unconditional synthesis, we enable training-free, zero-shot conditional generation via diffusion posterior sampling from image-derived prompts (e.g., sparse 3D points, slice contours, or partial surface patches), supporting interactive semi-automatic segmentation, editing and robust reconstruction under degraded imaging.

evidence.text: Accurate, patient-specific vascular geometry is pivotal for diagnosis, planning, and device design, yet existing statistical shape modeling (SSM) pipelines rely on linear priors and topology-specific preprocessing that limit realism, scalability, and interoperability.

Beyond unconditional synthesis, we enable training-free, zero-shot conditional generation via diffusion posterior sampling from image-derived prompts (e.g., sparse 3D points, slice contours, or partial surface patches), supporting interactive semi-automatic segmentation, editing and robust reconstruction under degraded imaging.
